question: Should this PR land the live Computer Use MCP probe exception, fail-closed readiness default, shared cache reconciliation, opt-in stale-child repair, health monitor, lease surface, and eight new config defaults together after the docs fix?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and well-proven, but it changes upgrade-visible defaults plus a sandbox-adjacent app-server call path and scoped host-process cleanup, which needs maintainer intent rather than automated correctness judgment.

options.title: Fix Docs And Approve Current Contract
options.body: Update the stale-child repair paragraph, then accept the stricter readiness, copied cache, direct probe exception, optional repair, optional health checks, lease primitive, and config defaults as the intended Computer Use contract.

options.title: Split Risky Surfaces
options.body: Land cache reconciliation and live status first, then review repair, health, lease, and broader config defaults in narrower follow-up PRs.

options.title: Narrow Defaults Before Merge
options.body: Preserve compatibility as the default and require explicit strict or repair settings until broader upgrade impact is proven.
